Crl.M.C No.4919 of 2022  2026:KER:27786  -3-  ORDER

(Dated this the 27th day of March, 2026) This is a petition filed under Section 482 Cr.PC, by the accused Nos.1 to 5 in Crime No.1184 of 2019 of Gandhi Nagar Police Station, Kottayam, which is pending as SC. No.136 of 2020 on the file of Additional District and Sessions Court-I(PoCSO),
Kottayam.
The offences alleged against them are under Sections 450, 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 4 r/w Section 3, 6 r/w Section 5(j)(ii), 21 r.w Section 19 of PoCSO Act.

2. The prosecution case is that the 1st accused, with an intention to satisfy his sexual lust by abusing the de facto complainant, who was a minor, made freiendship with her when she was studying in 9th standard, promised to marry her and trespassed into her residence on 23.12.2018 at about 12 noon,
committed penetrative sexual assault upon her and thereby she became pregnant.
It is also alleged that the accused persons 2 and 3, who are the parents of the 1st accused, failed to report the matter to the police.

3. According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, now the entire dispute between the petitioners and the de facto complainant has been settled, the 1 st petitioner married 2026:KER:27786 the de facto complainant and now they are living together as husband and wife along with their children.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.

4. The learned counsel for the de facto complainant/ 3rd respondent also submitted that the entire dispute between the petitioners and the de facto complainant has been settled, that the 1st petitioner married the de facto complainant and now they are living together as husband and wife along with Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214815/
2 their children.
5.
The petition was opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.

However, the learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions further submitted that the de facto complainant had given signed statement to the SHO, in tune with the averments in the affidavit filed by her before this Court.

6. The question whether a crime of aggravated penetrative sexual assault registered under the provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act could be quashed taking note of the fact that the victim was married by the accused was considered by a learned Single Judge of this Court in the decision in xxxx v. State of Kerala, 2025 (4) KHC 471.

entities.text: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: xxxx v. State of Kerala, 2025 (4) KHC 471
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
After relying upon various precedents, in paragraph 26 of the above decision, the learned Judge held that:
2026:KER:27786 (1) Unless the criminal proceedings are terminated by quashing the same, there will be utter chaos, confusion and even havoc in the life of the victim who married the accused, and who is leading a happy life.
In other words, the life of the victim, the accused and the child, if any, in that relationship will be ruined.
Per contra, If the offence is quashed, it will bring in harmony, peace and happiness, thus promoting their family life.
(2) Unless, the Court choose to quash the proceedings, the trauma/agony of the child/victim continues, despite a genuine and bonafide settlement.

(3) Despite and de-hors a bonafide and genuine settlement culminating in the marriage between the petitioner/accused and the victim, if the criminal proceedings are to continue - thereby compelling the parties to face the trial - the same verge upon abuse of process.
(4) The ends of justice is in favour of quashment in such category of cases, since it will be an injustice to separate a well knit family by the continuance of the proceedings.
(5) Quashment of the proceedings will result in rendering total and complete justice to the parties.

(6) When the crucial witness is the victim, who had married the accused, there exists little chance for her to speak against her own husband/ accused, wherefore, the chances of conviction will be too bleak and remote : 2025:KER:52904

In other words,
no fruitful purpose will be served by continuance of the proceedings.

(7) Compelling the continuance of a proceedings, which is otherwise settled genuinely and which answers the requirements of the interest of justice will only add to the burden of criminal courts in India, which is otherwise over burdened.
7. In the decision in Mahesh Mukund Patel v. State of U.P., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 614, the accused married the victim and they were leading a happy married life.

entities.text: Mahesh Mukund Patel v. State of U.P., 2025 SCC OnLine SC 614
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In that case also, the fact that the person who was once an assailant, now 2026:KER:27786 turned out to be the protector and saviour of the victim was considered as a relevant circumstance to quash the proceeding pending against Xxxxxx vs State Of Kerala on 27 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187214815/
3 him.
8. In this case also, the 1st petitioner has already married the victim on 19.10.2020 and now they are leading a happy married life.
To prove the same, the petitioner has produced a copy of the certificate of marriage issued by the Marriage Officer, Thalayazham, Kottayam.

In the affidavit filed by the victim she expressed her desire to terminate the prosecution proceedings against the petitioner and also that for preserving the peaceful and happy family life, termination of the proceedings is highly necessary.

9. Therefore, termination of the proceedings against the petitioners in such an exceptional circumstance is highly necessary to maintain the harmonious and peaceful life of the victim who now remains under the care and protection of the petitioner.
Therefore, the prayer for quashing the proceedings against the petitioners deserves favourable consideration.
10. In the result, this petition is allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioners/accused in Crime No.1184 of 2019 of Gandhi Nagar Police Station, Kottayam, which is pending 2026:KER:27786 as SC. No.136 of 2020 on the file of Additional District and Sessions Court-I(PoCSO), Kottayam, is hereby quashed under Section 482 Cr.PC.
